channel.title: IPD radar — capsid & nanomaterial design
channel.description: Weekly automated literature radar for protein design, self-assembly and structural machine learning.

item.title: RFOptimization: Guiding Design Optimization with All-Atom Structure Prediction
item.description:
Alternates gradient-guided mutation with an orthogonal structure predictor and MPNN redesign, so a binder has to survive a model it wasn't optimized against before it counts as improved.
Zhang, O., …, Baker, D. · bioRxiv · 7 Sep · design-method · action: read

item.title: Inverse FoldDir: Structure-conditioned Protein Sequence Design by Dirichlet Flow Matching
item.description:
Runs inverse folding as Dirichlet flow matching directly over the amino-acid simplex, so fixed-residue inpainting and soft biochemical preferences fall out of the same denoising process instead of needing separate machinery.
TARTICI, A., …, Wittmann, B. J. · bioRxiv · 7 Sep · design-method · action: read

item.title: A rugged binding landscape unifies static and dynamic paradigms in protein-protein interactions
item.description:
Two nanobody series bind their antigens the same way but for different reasons: one obeys Rosetta scoring of the crystal structure, the other only ranks correctly once the interface is allowed to move in MD.
Liu, T., …, Sun, B. · bioRxiv · 4 Sep · struct-pred · action: read · touches: oracles predicting whether a designed subunit assembles, without experimental positives

item.title: ABAG-Rank: Improving Model Selection of AlphaFold Antibody-Antigen Complexes by Learning to Rank.
item.description:
A permutation-invariant DeepSets ranker picks the right antibody-antigen decoy out of an AF ensemble, indifferent to how many candidates you hand it.
Tadiello M, …, Elofsson A · Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) · 4 Sep · struct-pred · action: skim

item.title: Ensemble tests mask missing dynamics in protein conformational generators
item.description:
Randomly shuffle the frames of a real MD trajectory and it still passes the field's standard ensemble-fidelity test — the metric can't distinguish learned dynamics from a slideshow.
Liu, K., …, Chi, Y. · bioRxiv · 4 Sep · ml-method · action: read

item.title: The fitness landscape of a form II rubisco in a photosynthetic bacterium guides engineering of oxygen tolerance.
item.description:
A 15,000-variant fitness screen plus a trained transformer turns rubisco's oxygen-tolerance problem into a recombination search over real fitness data, not a hand-picked hotspot list.
Hoffmann UA, …, Hudson EP · Science advances · 4 Sep · enzyme · action: skim · touches: negative-example construction for design-quality regression

item.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence.
item.description:
Contrastive learning on protein language model embeddings finds catalytic residues from sequence alone, beating methods that require a crystal structure.
Rieger WJF, …, Mora A · eLife · 4 Sep · enzyme · action: read

item.title: BAGEL-CAR: Reflections on the Bits to Binders Competition
item.description:
Their winning CAR binders were never refolded before submission — apply the standard ESMFold refiltering step after the fact and every experimentally enriched hit would have been thrown out.
Lala, J., Angioletti-Uberti, S. · bioRxiv · 4 Sep · function-design · action: read · touches: negative-example construction for design-quality regression

item.title: ProRB: a structure-free unified framework for joint prediction and design of protein-RNA interactions.
item.description:
One sequence-only model both scores protein-RNA affinity and generates the RNA that binds your protein, with cross-attention maps that read out the motif it learned.
Xue Y, …, Pan X · Nucleic acids research · 7 Sep · function-design · action: read

item.title: Learning Universal Representations of Intermolecular Interactions with ATOMICA
item.description:
Pretrains one geometric model on two million interaction complexes so the same embeddings zero-shot-prioritize binding residues across proteins, ligands, metals and nucleic acids.
Fang, A., …, Zitnik, M. · bioRxiv · 7 Sep · ml-method · action: read · touches: oracles predicting whether a designed subunit assembles, without experimental positives

item.title: The elasticity of semiflexible polymers with reversible spontaneous curvature in two dimensions
item.description:
Models a semiflexible polymer as a two-state system where an uncurved and a curved conformation compete, with the state populated according to an activation-energy-controlled equilibrium rather than being fixed by chain identity.
BLINDSPOT · Donghyeon Kim, Panayotis Benetatos · arXiv · 4 Sep · struct-pred · action: track

item.title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies.
item.description:
Over a hundred designed protein shells that move RNA orders of magnitude better than lipid nanoparticles, retargeted by grafting on a different designed peptide binder — and carried all the way to a pig gene-editing model.
Schuhmacher MK, …, Wurst W · Nature · 2 Sep · assembly · action: read · touches: symmetry-native / tied-ASU diffusion for icosahedral assemblies

item.title: Design of peptides with non-canonical amino acids using flow matching
item.description:
Describes a non-canonical amino acid by its atoms and bonds instead of as a fixed token, so it can place residues it never saw in training — and beats AlphaFold3-based methods at predicting them.
Jin Sub Lee, Philip M. Kim · Bioinformatics · 31 Aug · design-method · action: read

item.title: Programmable design of synthetic plant immune receptors for pathogen protein recognition.
item.description:
Grafts a de novo binder into a plant immune receptor's decoy domain and then evolves it in planta, because binding the pathogen protein and correctly firing the receptor turn out to be two different problems.
Zhu H, …, Gao C · Science (New York, N.Y.) · 3 Sep · function-design · action: read

item.title: Lenacapavir allosterically remodels the HIV-1 capsid.
item.description:
Destabilises the capsid's high-curvature pentameric vertices first and lets failure cascade from there — the opposite of the lattice-hyperstabiliser story, and a map of where a small interface change gets amplified into whole-shell collapse.
Dos Santos NFB, …, Pornillos O · Science advances · 2 Sep · assembly · action: read · touches: symmetry-native / tied-ASU diffusion for icosahedral assemblies

item.title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles
item.description:
One designed pocket that reversibly binds a whole family of rhodamines rather than a bespoke pocket per dye, which is what buys it brighter STED than HaloTag — and it still works at 75 °C.
Yuda Chen, …, Bo Huang · Cell · 1 Sep · function-design · action: read

item.title: Toward De Novo Protein Design from Natural Language
item.description:
A 16B-parameter model that turns a free-text functional description straight into a sequence, with designed enzymes that actually turn over; everything shown is monomeric, so whether text can steer a symmetric assembly is untested.
Dai, F., …, Yuan, F. · bioRxiv · 31 Aug · design-method · action: read

item.title: Hierarchical discrete representations for coarse-to-fine protein conformation generation.
item.description:
Fixes global topology in a coarse code and refines local geometry conditioned on it, keeping conformational diversity without losing validity — the coarse/fine split is worth stealing for quasi-equivalence, one fold code with per-slot refinements.
On S, …, Kim ES · Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) · 31 Aug · struct-pred · action: read · touches: quasi-equivalence: one sequence, multiple backbone conformations by assembly slot

item.title: Design and characterization of broadly protective influenza A(H3N2) vaccine candidates using protein language models
item.description:
A language model proposes HA variants and a learned antigenic-distance model picks which to build; two of seven protected against strains that did not yet exist when they were designed — a generate-and-score loop that worked with no wet-lab positives.
Howard, V. R., …, Georgiev, I. S. · bioRxiv · 31 Aug · immunogen · action: read · touches: oracles predicting whether a designed subunit assembles, without experimental positives

item.title: De novo design of CR2 binder as vaccine scaffold
item.description:
A designed, stable, high-affinity binder to the B-cell co-receptor CR2 in place of native C3d — the adjuvant becomes the designed protein itself rather than something added to the formulation.
Liu, Y.-T., …, Sun, C. · bioRxiv · 3 Sep · immunogen · action: read

item.title: Pyridoxal photoenzymes for asymmetric radical-radical cross-couplings.
item.description:
Makes pyridoxal phosphate a photocatalyst by using its excited-state quinonoid as a strong single-electron reductant, opening a cofactor 'dark space' that photoenzyme design had never touched.
Sorensen CC, …, Hyster TK · Nature · 27 Jul · enzyme · action: skim

item.title: Anomalous temperature dependence in phase transitions via ballistic coalescence
item.description:
Clusters that move ballistically rather than diffusively switch from algebraic to explosively fast growth, and the temperature at which they cross over is non-monotonic — the growth law itself changes class.
BLINDSPOT · Nalina Vadakkayil, …, Subir K. Das · arXiv · 31 Aug · ml-method · action: track
